title: Finite constrained segmentation: derivation, exact method and experiment
description: Develop a reviewable known-result analysis, not a novel statistical claim. For a finite T-by-d signal y with T,d positive, choose K internal breakpoints, each positive multiple of jump, so every segment has length at least min_size. Include T as the final endpoint even if T is not a grid multiple. Minimize the sum, over all segments and coordinates, of squared deviations from each segment's coordinate mean. Derive why the mean solves the within-segment least-squares problem and establish a globally optimal finite procedure with an explicit argument, assumptions, infeasibility handling, ties and restricted-grid scope. Do not claim consistency, unknown-K selection or guaranteed recovery of physical changes. Implement your own Python procedure with the frozen run_estimator interface below; published author code and operator answers are not supplied. Investigate its behavior using a second, fully specified experiment: T=6,d=1, true means (0,0,0,1,1,1), independent noise at each observation equally likely -1 or +1, K=1,min_size=2,jump=1. Estimate or exactly integrate the expected minimized unnormalized total squared-deviation objective. Supply actual model-authored executable experiment source and results, including evaluation_mode ('exact_enumeration' or 'monte_carlo'), objective_values, mean_objective, mcse, and n_cases. In exact mode list one value for every equally likely noise vector and report mcse=0; in Monte Carlo mode use independently generated noise vectors, fix the future count before confirmation, report the usual standard error of the sample mean, and target mcse <=0.02. Choose and justify your own implementation, diagnostic tests and internal acceptance criteria. The source-first execution ABI additionally returns acceptance_passed (boolean) and requested_runtime_replicates (positive integer); confirmation uses that source-declared count. Use durable Markdown/LaTeX for the derivation, explain discrepancies honestly and submit only your selected final artifacts. Formalization is not requested. Permitted source background: Truong, Oudre and Vayatis, Selective review of offline change point detection methods, Signal Processing 167:107299 (2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00718v3. This closed-source-access development task supplies its mathematical definitions directly; it is not full-paper reproduction, blind rediscovery or a test of literature search.

request_fields.name: signal
request_fields.meaning: Observed rectangular finite-valued signal, rows in time order
request_fields.shape: T by d, T>=1 and d>=1
request_fields.indexing: Zero-based Python rows; endpoint b includes rows 0 through b-1
request_fields.edge_cases: Constant and multivariate signals are valid

request_fields.name: n_changes
request_fields.meaning: Number K of internal breakpoints, not number of segments
request_fields.indexing: There are K+1 segments when feasible
request_fields.edge_cases: K=0 is valid; excessive K may be infeasible

request_fields.name: min_size
request_fields.meaning: Minimum length of every segment including the first and last
request_fields.indexing: Segment length equals end minus start
request_fields.edge_cases: min_size=1 is supported; values larger than T are infeasible

request_fields.name: jump
request_fields.meaning: Spacing of the grid of admissible internal endpoints
request_fields.indexing: Internal endpoints are jump, 2*jump, ... below T
request_fields.edge_cases: The final endpoint T is never required to be a grid multiple

response_fields.name: feasible
response_fields.indexing: Refers to the whole supplied request
response_fields.edge_cases: Return false rather than substitute a different K or grid

response_fields.name: breakpoints
response_fields.meaning: An attaining admissible endpoint tuple including T when feasible
response_fields.shape: K+1 strictly increasing integer endpoints if feasible, otherwise empty
response_fields.indexing: First segment starts at zero; final endpoint is T
response_fields.edge_cases: Any exact minimizing tie is accepted; infeasible returns []

response_fields.name: objective
response_fields.meaning: Minimized sum of within-segment squared deviations across all coordinates
response_fields.indexing: Sum over all rows and coordinates of returned segments
response_fields.edge_cases: Zero is valid; null only for infeasibility
response_fields.normalization: Unnormalized total sum, not divided by T or d

invariants.meaning: Return a global optimum over exactly the supplied min_size and grid, not an unconstrained or greedy substitute

empirical_claims.meaning: Expected minimized unnormalized objective under the explicitly supplied six-observation finite noise experiment
